rv.q: This is one of those canonical musicals that now works better as a concert, the score unencumbered from paper-thin characters and insufficient story.
Director Sasha Gerritson has staged and guided a phenomenal Chicagoland production that’s an absolute must-see experience.

So yes it is a silly play with some lovely tunes, simple fairytale set and costumes, with some great moments about the human condition that ring emotionally true, and perhaps most importantly, very well done by Musical Theater Works.

Solid serenading and energetic choreography guide us down the winding path to the otherworldly village of Brigadoon, whisking an audience away from the cares of everyday life and into an alternate reality.
For today escapism is appropriate, and "Brigadoon" delivers!
In fact, the biggest problem with Brigadoon is that it’s a fairly slight story, with glancing tragicomic overtones, stuffed into an overlong show.
Brigadoon brings back the glorious moments of Broadway in an evening you will long remember.
This production brings back memories from many years ago.

cn.t: Critics find this Music Theater Works production enchanting, praising Loewe's lush score and romantic fantasy elements, though some note the 1947 show's dated story and shallow characters haven't aged well.
